tools.description: App-specific relevance (0–100) of up to 100 keywords for a tracked app, from the same scorer as the UI. Returns at once with ready, pending, failed or unavailable for each keyword. Pending is not zero: call again after 3 seconds or more, backing off. retry=true retries failed work after its cooldown

tools.name: evaluate_keywords
tools.description: Rank and classify candidate keywords by Asonix popularity, difficulty and opportunity. Use it before recommending keywords or calling add_keywords. Known keywords reuse stored scores; up to 20 new ones per call are scored privately, without adding them to public research. Pass popularityScore and di

tools.description: Who ranks for a keyword in one storefront; appStoreId gives that app's rank. Uses results Asonix checked in the last 18 hours, else a private live check; saves nothing. Adds stored scores when Asonix has them; to score a new keyword, use evaluate_keywords. To find an app by name, use search_apps. ru

tools.name: get_app_search_ads_keywords

Asonix checks each keyword about once a day, so a missing keyword may still be bid on. observedSharePercent7d is the share of the last 7 days' checks that showed the ad, not impression share.

tools.name: get_keyword_history
tools.description: Return keyword popularity or difficulty history for an Asonix keyword, with cached topAdvertisers for eligible iOS keywords. Pending advertiser observations are queued; retry later.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "check_tracked_keywords" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

evidence.snippet: Check candidate keyword terms against one tracked app's existing tracked keywords without dumping the full keyword table. iOS keyword rows include cached topAdv…

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search_apps · Private data: create_unreleased_app, get_workspace_keyword_opportunities, check_tracked_keywords, get_app_rating_history, extract_competitor_keywords, get_keyword_top_apps · Public sink: get_app_search_ads_keywords · Destructive: get_ai_visibility_overview, get_ai_visibility_evidence, unstar_keyword.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search_apps · Private data: create_unreleased_app, get_workspace_keyword_opportunities, check_tracked_keywords, get_app_rating_history, extract_competitor_keywords, get_keyword_top_apps · Public sink: get_app_search_ads_keywords · Destructive: get_ai_visibility_overview, get_ai_visibility_evidence, unstar_keyword

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
